subject: Human Evolution
title: Hand Stencils
description: Learn Hand Stencils in one minute.

hook.text: Deep in a cave, someone placed a hand on the wall and blew pigment around it. The hand is still there.

buildup.text: Hand stencils are among the most common and oldest cave art—found from Indonesia to Patagonia.

discovery.text: They say 'I was here.' Across 40,000 years, the urge to leave a personal mark hasn't changed.

twist.text: Many stencils show missing fingers. Ritual amputation? Frostbite? Finger folding for sign language?

climax.text: These hands connect us directly to individual ice age people—a message across impossible time.

punchline.text: A handprint is the oldest selfie.

quiz.question: What makes hand stencils significant in cave art?
options: They're personal marks found globally across 40,000 years
